text.p: The Czech Republic and Poland will sign a transportation memorandum in Prague on Friday, in an attempt to help the flow of combined highway-rail transport between the two countries.

"The memorandum, which will lay the ground for the existance of combined transportation between Poland and the Czech Republic, will be signed tomorrow," Matin Riman, Czech Transportation Minister, told Reuters on Thursday.
"It will be the first grade of negotiation," he added.
Riman declined to provide further details before the treaty signing with his Polish counterpart Boguslaw Liberadzky, who is currently visiting the Czech Republic.
A trans-European north-south corridor route is also on the agenda for the meeting, but Riman declined to comment on it.
"We are in negotiatians also with other countries involved in the route...We will start construction next year, but only next year's European-wide conference in Helsinki will decide," Riman said.
The Czech Republic faces hot competition with its former federatioon partner, Slovakia, to have the corridor cross their territory.
The Czech government has recently agreed to accelerate spending on new motorway construction, with a plan to build a new 485 km highway costing 120 billion crowns through the year 2002.
